description:
FILED s464aw while shipping #972 (the bitwise overload dispatch), probed
5.40.3 vs ./runpcl on the s464aw tree AFTER #972.

perl dispatches `use overload' under `use integer' exactly as it does outside
it -- probed, one class per row:

    package OB; use overload q/|/ => sub {"OR"}, q/<</ => sub {"SHL"},
                             q(0+) => sub {42}, q("") => sub {"OB"};
    { use integer;
      $b | 3     perl OR    PCL 43
      $b << 3    perl SHL   PCL 336 }

PCL cannot dispatch there because `use integer' does not call the runtime op
at all: `Pl/ExprToCL.pm' emits CL PRIMITIVES inline (lines ~1592-1604 and
~3103), a THIRD copy of the arithmetic and bitwise semantics beside the
runtime's:

    +  -  *      ->  (+ (p-int L) (p-int R))            etc.
    /            ->  (truncate (p-int L) (p-int R))
    %            ->  (rem ...)
    &  |  ^      ->  (p-to-s64 (logand|logior|logxor (%pcl-to-integer (to-number L)) ...))
    ~            ->  (p-to-s64 (lognot (%pcl-to-integer (to-number ...))))
    << >>        ->  (p-<<-int L R) / (p->>-int L R)    <- runtime functions,
                                                          but they have no
                                                          overload dispatch
                                                          either

So EVERY overloadable operator loses its dispatch inside a `use integer'
scope, and the two that do reach the runtime lose it for the other reason.

WHY #972 DID NOT FIX IT.  #972 is a `cl/'-only change; this needs the
EMISSION to route through runtime functions (`p-+-int', `p-bit-or-int', ...
which do not exist), i.e. a `Pl/' change with corpus-diff + a generation bump
+ artifact regeneration.  Adding dispatch to `p-<<-int'/`p->>-int' alone was
considered and REJECTED: it would make the family answer inconsistently
(`<<' dispatching while `|' in the same block does not), and the honest unit
is "`use integer' is a third semantics copy".

BAR: the two probe rows above plus one per operator; corpus-diff (a `Pl/'
change); the sweep; a guard in Pl/t/overload-01.t.  NOTE `op/overload_integer.t`
in the companion is OK 2/0 today and must stay so.
subject: use integer bypasses ALL operator overloading (the ops are emitted inline)
